description:
Here’s a pull-up technique tutorial to smoothen out your reps.

1. Pull your shoulder blades down your back and hold them in place throughout the pull-up.

2. Use a slightly wider grip, pulling your elbows towards your sides.

3. Aim to pull vertically instead of pulling back, then into the bar.

4. Use the front of your core to form a hollow body shape instead of using your lower back.

title: RDL Tips
description:
When performing a RDL, going lower is not always better. Once your hip hinge range of motion reaches its limit, you should stop descending. If you go beyond the range that your gluteus maximus and hamstrings can actively control, the excess movement will be compensated by your lower back (erector spinae), leading to unnecessary stress on the lumbar spine. This is a common reason why many people experience lower back pain during RDLs.

✅ The PERFECT Barbell Squat

1️⃣ Keep your knees in line with your toes — don’t let them cave in as you rise.
2️⃣ The bar should stay over your midfoot — leaning too far forward pushes it ahead of your center of gravity and throws off your balance.
3️⃣ Point your elbows slightly back and down to keep the bar tight — not straight back.
4️⃣ Keep your entire foot planted throughout the movement — avoid lifting your heels.

title: Quick guide how to start and stop on the cycling rollers. Follow for more cycling tips.
description:
How to: Start and stop on the rollers:
1. With a support of one leg on the ground or rollers frame, start spinning the pedals with the other leg. 
2. After few spins, wheels will start acting as gyroscopes and the bike will be stable.
3. Hop on the saddle, start spinning as normal. 
4. To stop - unclip one feet as usual and while wheels are still spinning put it on the ground or frame. 
5. Unclip the second leg and you’re done!

Efficiency always beats symmetry.

Start with your weight equal between your knees and your hands. Tilt your pelvis back to clench your abs as much as you can. 

Contract your glutes to push your hips forward and down so you shift your weight onto your hands. 

Maintain tension in the abs and glutes as you flex your shoulders to roll your hands forward. 

Pull back using your lats while keeping your hips and core locked.

title: How to Avoid Cross-Contamination with Gluten-free Baking for Celiac Disease #glutenfreerecipes
description:
Tag your friend with Celiac disease so they can share this post. Let’s raise awareness about avoiding gluten cross-contamination!

Celiac disease is an autoimmune disease which is triggered by ingesting gluten. Gluten is a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye.

As little as an 1/8th of a teaspoon of flour contains enough gluten to trigger the autoimmune response in someone with Celiac disease.

When that happens, the body (incorrectly) attacks its own cells - which causes damage to the small

title: Kitchen Hack: Lining a Round Cake Pan! #kitchenhacks #momhacks #bakinghacks
description:
By far the easiest way to line your round cake pans and ensure that your cakes come out ✨ PERFECT ✨

Fold your parchment paper into a point. Then measure from the centre of the BOTTOM of the pan to the edge, and then a bit extra for the sides. Cut alone that crease you made. Then make 2 cuts about 1/3 down, unfold and press into the pan! 🎂

It’s as easy as that! 😃

description:
You’ll need:
fresh strawberries
2 ripe bananas
melted dark chocolate

1. Line a glass container with strawberries.
2. Blend together bananas and melted chocolate.
3. Pour the chocolate banana mixture over the strawberries.
4. Let set in the freezer until solid (about 4 hours).
5. Remove from the freezer, slice and enjoy! ❤️

title: The Basics of Sautéing Correctly!
description:
1. Empty pan on Medium-High heat
2. Wait until hot -- use the water test and wait for it to *dance*
3. Oil in
4. Wait a few seconds then put in whatever you are cooking
5. WAIT! Let it sit. Don't fidget, and definitely DO NOT CROWD THE PAN
6. Flip and continue to cook on the other side until you are satisfied!

What's the difference between a sauté and a sear? Not much... a sear is pretty much the same just with a bit more of browning (from cooking longer or using a higher heat).

SAVE THIS FOR THE NEXT TIME YOU MAKE RICE!

•2 cups rice, I prefer using long grain basmati
•4 cups water (if you need measurements)
•1 tsp salt
•1 tsp avocado oil 

1️⃣Place your rice in a stockpot & rinse it 6-10 times until the water runs clear.
2️⃣Add enough COLD water to cover the rice from the tip of your fingernail, to the bottom of your fingertip (video shows you).
3️⃣Add salt & oil, bring to a boil. Once boiling, lower the heat to low, cover with a lid and let it simmer for 10 minutes.

It is important to differentiate between the two in order to choose the correct treatment. 

▪️Acne Marks: 
Marks are either red or dark brown in colour. There is no change in texture of skin or depression. 
These can be treated with creams containing skin lightening agents such as azleaic acid, kojic acid, alpha arbutin and niacinamide.

title: Is Anti-aging skin care a scam ?
description:
✨Anti-aging creams don’t stop aging
As a dermatologist, I remind my patients that these creams cannot reach the deeper layers where collagen & fat loss truly happen. That’s why they can’t prevent sagging or reverse structural aging.

But don’t dismiss them! 

They do improve skin texture, hydration, fine lines & overall glow — making your skin look healthier and more radiant.

Think of them as skin quality enhancers, not age erasers.

title:
These are the 5 steps to unlock any calisthenics skill:

1. Master the starting position.

Build strength, stability, and connective tissue by perfecting the foundation of the exercise. High plank for pushups, active hang for pullups, dip support hold for dips, and so on.

2. Introduce limited range.

Use partial reps to build strength in controlled ranges of motion. Progressively expand the range over time instead of repeating the same limited movement forever.

3. Use negatives.

Slow and controlled eccentrics are one of the most effective ways to unlock new exercises and build control through full range.

4. Build concentric strength.

Once negatives become clean and controlled, begin building the full movement through quality repetitions and assisted variations.

5. Increase the range.

After achieving around 8 clean full ROM reps, start increasing range further through deficit variations and deeper range exercises.

Treat this as a framework, not a rigid rule set.

title:
Unlock the 🔥 ELBOW LEVER 🔥 and level up your calisthenics game 💪

Here’s how to do it step-by-step 👇

1️⃣ Hand placement matters
Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the ground, fingers pointing forward or slightly out 🤲

2️⃣ Elbows into your core
Lean forward and drive your elbows into your stomach/hips area — this is your “shelf” 🧱

3️⃣ Shift your weight forward
Slowly lean your shoulders past your hands… this is KEY ⚖️
The more you lean, the lighter your legs feel

4️⃣ Lift one leg at a time
Start by lifting one foot, then the other 🦵
Don’t rush — control is everything

5️⃣ Engage EVERYTHING
Squeeze your core, glutes, and legs tight 🧠➡️💪
Stay as still as possible like a statue 🗿

💡 Pro tip: Start with bent knees if straight legs are too hard — build strength first, then extend later!

Consistency + control = mastery 🚀

Straight arms, core tension, feet angle and posterior pelvic tilt.

Master the fundamentals, and the full skill will come.

title:
STRONG FOR SUMMER - HOME WORKOUT 

50 sec work, 20 sec rest 

heavy as you can go with perfect form

1. Heels elevated goblet squat
2. Reverse lunge left (glute bias - lean forward!)
3. Reverse lunge left (glute bias - lean forward!)
4. Lateral raises (crispy shoulders)
5. Tricep pushups (Hands under shoulders - shoot elbows back towards hips and bring chest forward to target back of arms)
6. Glute Bridge (banded + weighted) Go heavy! For these: do 50 sec bridge, 20 sec pulse. Then rest. Thank me later.
7. Tuck-in crunch or Jackknife - Pick your poison! Both HURT! Make sure your shoulders lift off the floor, and your hips pull in slightly for full engagement of your abs.

Give yourself 2-3 hard working sets of each, 3x a week. 

Repeating the same movement patterns and getting stronger at them is what brings results.

Go get em!

title:
This is as simple and efficient as it gets.
Just two movements. Don't underestimate it.

400 reps in 20 minutes.

Minute 1: 10 sit-up burpees
Minute 2: 30 push-ups
Repeat.

That's 100 sit-up burpees and 300 push-ups total.

You'll probably need to scale this-and that's fine.

Lower the push-up reps. Modify the burpees. Most people can't do sit-up burpees clean because they require real core strength, foot/ankle mobility, hip power, and coordination to explode out of a deep squat.

But once you can do them, that's a massive sign your body is working the way it should.

Springy. Elastic. Mobile. Athletic.

That's the goal.

Not just looking good in the mirror.
Not just curling and pressing weights.
But moving well.

You don't need to be a circus freak.
You don't need backflips or extreme flexibility.

The real goal is restoring childlike movement capacity.
You used to be able to do this. Every kid can.

Losing that should be unacceptable.

That's why I love routines like this-you get shredded, conditioned, and athletic at the same time. You don't just look fit. You move like it.

If you want me to personally help you rebuild this-training, fasting, accountability, direct access to me - hit that link in bio and we shall talk soon🫡

I started honouring the body God blessed me with and asked Him for the strength and courage to keep going… Now I’m stronger, healthier and more confident than I’ve EVER been before & I strive to keep improving every single day.
This community genuinely inspires me so much and I want you to know that wherever you’re at on your own fitness journey, even if it feels like there’s no one there to support you, I’ll be here and my DMs are always open 🫶

If you ever need additional support my 1:1 coaching application is in my b!o ☺️

Lysm, Soph xx

title:
Hiiiiiii
This is a real body and a real transformation. Around 15-17 pounds lost (more to come) within 4 months. I DID THAT. Little progress is STILL progress. 
I’ve been called big, ugly, fat, and genuinely allllll of the names you can think of by people I do know and people I don’t know. Quite frankly, these terrible words were used by people I wouldn’t never want to switch lives with…
I’ve been on my grind. In school (4.0 gpa AND awarded for my “consistency and excellence”) in work, in the gym (15-17lbs lost and more to go) and in my social life. My life is good. I have an amazing support system. I am grateful for the life that I am so blessed to live. 
This is your reminder that baby steps are still steps and that small progress is still progress. Do NOT give up on yourself just because people are hating. Prove to them and most importantly, yourself,  that you are capable of hard things. YOU GOT THIS.
Being from a small city, I know word travels quickly. So to the people who used to put me down, hi, hello, hope you’re well and I hope you enjoy this transformation as much as I do !!!! Mind you, this is just the beginning. Xoxo 
😊😊😊💗💗💗

HIIT training done in most gym classes isn’t proper HIIT. It’s more like high intensity moderately steady state cardio.

Proper HIIT is SAVAGE!

An example of proper HIIT training would be on a bike / assault bike / rower / running perform

30s max effort 
Rest 90 seconds
Repeat 5-10 times

Your performance will significantly drop across the efforts
You will be gasping for air
You should be recovering quite a lot between reps

title:
Stop with all the H.I.I.T training!

H.I.I.T stands for high intensity interval training.

It consists of short burst of high intensity exercise that may or may not include resistance (weights).

It’s a very enticing option because of the fact that it can burn so many calories in a short period of time. 

But that’s precisely where the issue lies. You see, we should not select our method of exercise based off of how many calories it burns. 

Rather, we should focus on trying to build muscle which plays a critical role in our body composition, overall health, and ultimately whether we lose body fat and keep it off. 

The fact is that HIIT training is not optimal for building muscle due primarily to low levels of tension and time under tension on the muscle during the exercises amongst other things. 

To build muscle, we need to choose exercises that are stable where we can produce as much force as possible, that we can progressively overload or increase the weight on over time, and where we can slow down and control the weight the entire time to maintain tension rather than trying to move as quickly as possible. 

If you like this information, save it for later and share with another busy parent trying to get in shape 💪🏽

#fitness #fitdad #fitmom #weightloss #homeworkout #healthylifestyle #fitnessmotivation

title:
🔥 What is HIIT?

HIIT = High-Intensity Interval Training.

It’s short bursts of hard effort followed by quick recovery periods.

Think:
30–40 seconds of work
20–30 seconds of rest
Repeat 🔁

Why people love it:
✔ Efficient (done in 20–30 minutes)
✔ Boosts endurance + power
✔ Burns calories during and after
✔ Builds mental grit

It’s not about going long.
It’s about going intentional.

Short. Strong. Effective. 🔥

title:
✨Try this steady slow flow✨

There can be a tendency in practice to rush through the transitions, anticipating the next posture before we’ve fully arrived in the one we’re in. But so much lives in the space between the shapes, in the transitions. 

A steady pace gives us the opportunity to notice what is actually happening beneath the surface. Not to bypass discomfort or force our way through it, but to stay connected to the experience as it unfolds.

As Alan Watts said, “The thing you must do with all the feelings you dislike is experience them as deeply as possible.”

This practice is an invitation to stay with yourself through each transition, each sensation, each breath.

Practice with me on @innerdimensionyoga

title:
do these and notice how much better your body feels 🥰🫶🏻

these are the poses I return to almost every day, either on their own or into my flows.

they’re simple, but powerful. they help me stay connected to my body, release tension from sitting, and keep my practice grounded.

𖦹 Uttanasana (1 Minute)
calms the nervous system & releases tension through the entire back body

𖦹 Cat-Cow (5 rounds, listen to your body)
keeps my spine mobile & releases stiffness from daily sitting

𖦹 Low Lunge → Half Split (8 rounds each side)
opens hips & hamstrings and creates space after long hours in one position

𖦹 Pigeon Pose (hold for 1-3 minutes)
deep hip release where I let go of physical & emotional tension

𖦹 Cobra Lifts (5 rounds)
opens the heart & strengthens the spine for better posture

𖦹 Supine Twist (hold as long as you like - i‘ll normally do 1-3 minutes)
resets my spine & helps my whole system unwind

& now… hug yourself 🤍
have a beautiful, energizing day ✨

#yogaflow #dailyasanas #dailypractice #mobilityexercises #yogaforeveryone

This flow is truly meant for a vinyasa class – when piecing it together I was really thinking about postures that felt natural in the body when linked together. 

I was inspired by the element of water. How water can be such a force, but also so adaptable, gentle, life-giving.

The sanskrit word “vinyasa” comes from the root words Vi meaning ‘in a special way’ and Nyasa meaning ‘to place,’ so Vinyasa can be translated as~ to place in a special way.

This flow today is really one you should feel in your body. I hope you try it, and I hope you enjoy it my friends.

title:
👀 FLEXIBLE HIPS & HAMSTRINGS 😍
 (Intermediate)

This hip and hamstring mobility flow blends strength, length, and mindful control. Each movement invites you to open gradually, protect your low back, and move from your center. Expect deep hip work, supported hamstring lengthening, and smooth transitions that build functional flexibility and ease.

⚠️Stop if you have pain. Always consult your healthcare provider before starting any exercise program.

1. Malasana Mobility: Come into Malasana with your spine tall and chest lifted. Shift to one side as you bend a knee inward, grounding through the opposite heel, then return to center and switch. Keep the movement fluid and breathe steadily, staying upright and avoiding strain in the knees.

2. Low Squat → Forearm Press:Start in a low squat with your forearms grounded. Press firmly through your forearms, draw your ribs in, and keep your core active. Straighten your legs as you lift the hips up and back. Maintain a long spine, engaged shoulders, and steady breath as you move in and out with control.

3. Lunge → Half Split: A deep hip and hamstring opener. Keep your spine straight as you tip forward from the hips, bending the straight-leg knee as needed to protect your hamstrings and low back. Avoid rounding your back, and keep your front knee aligned over your ankle for stability. Move slowly and stay connected to your breath.

4. One-Legged Down Dog → Straddle Sweep: From One-Legged Down Dog, sweep your lifted leg gently across into a wide-leg straddle, opening hips and hamstrings with control. Keep a soft bend in the standing knee, press evenly through both hands, and maintain a straight, neutral spine to protect your low back. Rotate from the hip joint (not the knee), land lightly with toes active, and bend the knees anytime you need more support. Move with your breath and prioritize control over depth.

title:
The most efficient way to improve your strength & build muscle in the gym is implementing progressive overload.

You can do this my changing 3 variables within your training.

1.) Volume - increasing or decreasing the amount of reps your doing to force your body to adapt.

2.) Intensity - To intensify your workouts you can decrease your rest time, implement more drop sets and super sets!

3.) Load - Increasing the amount of weight your using progressively. The goal is to force your muscle to adapt to the new amount of stress being put on the body!

If you want to see some serious body composition changes you need to implementing progressive overload.

You can’t go in the gym without a plan, wing it & expect to get great results. It’s not going to happen.❌

The only way to take your results to the next level is have structure with what your doing with a clear vision of what you want to accomplish!

This circuit teaches the core to create tension so your arms can move with power without your spine compensating. Stability first. Strength follows.

Circuit 2: 3 rounds
* ﻿﻿Push-up to down dog :8 reps
* ﻿﻿Inverted barbell holds : 30 seconds (modify with knees bent).
* ﻿﻿Tall kneeling lateral raises : 8reps

Time under tension improves muscle endurance and joint integrity, while the kneeling position forces the core and glutes to support the spine. Strong shoulders need a stable base.

Circuit 3: 3 rounds
* ﻿﻿Tall Kneeling Band pull-aparts : 10reps
* ﻿﻿Single-arm kickbacks: 8reps per side
* ﻿﻿Knees-elevated cat cow: 12 reps
* 
This circuit restores alignment, integrates breath with movement, and brings the nervous system back into balance so recovery actually happens.

This is how you build a body that's strong, stable, and resilient for life.
Save this workout. Train with purpose.

title:
Episode 4: So like, what is strength training?

Strength training is having a moment right now ❤️‍🔥 Everyone knows they NEED muscle and I’m here to teach you how to build it. It’s quite simple. I believe everyone should learn the foundational lifts: squat, bench, overhead press, and deadlift. Ps those are compound lifts.

You need to learn how to do them safely. You need to learn how to lift an appropriate weight, rest between sets, and repeat it (a lot).

You don’t change everything every week. You make small (boring lol) progressions and you track it. It’s that simple! Swap 3 random workouts you do each week for strength training and you’ll feel, look, and perform better.

title:
Full body strength & conditioning workout!! Why get smaller this summer when you can get athletic? 🫦

Workout (level: intermediate)

Superset:
1a) Tempo landmine RDLs - 3 sets of 8. Tempo just means slow on the eccentric (way down in this case) and fast on the way up. 3 seconds down, 1 second up
1b) Kneeling DB press with banded row - 3 sets of 8 per side. I prefer to be explosive with these but do what feels right for you

Superset:
2a) Barbell drive step ups - 3 sets of 5 per side. Go as heavy as you can WHILE maintaining power & speed. Box is a bit shorter than what you would use for regular step ups to allow you room to drive up & have a powerful plant of the working foot.
2b) Shortened copenhagen plank - 3 sets of 20 secs per side.

Contrast superset:
3а) Push ups 3 sets of 5. Rest for 20-30 seconds then:
3b) Explosive plyo push ups (band assisted) 3 sets of 3-5 reps. Make it bouncy!!!

4. Standing cable rotation - 3 sets of 8 per side. If youre anything like me, your arms will want to take over but make sure your core is doing the heavy lifting here!!

5. Sprint intervals 80% - 20 secs on, 1 minute off. 6 rounds. If you need more rest in order to hit that 80% output on every round, then take it!!

Wearing @Oner Active enhancelift - most worn collection everrrr.

#fullbodyworkout #fullbody #functionaltraining #functionalworkout #athletictraining

title:
Kettlebell workout of the day! 🚨 99% of people training “core” are doing it WRONG… 🚨
SAVE THIS… because most of you won’t finish it. SHARE this with someone who says they train “core” but never does THIS…

I rebuilt my body from double hip replacement… not with machines… but by relearning how to move, stabilize, and produce power again.

And this is the difference:

Most people train muscles…
Athletes train rotation, control, and force.

Do 80 reps a week of these and watch what happens:

→ your waist tightens without endless crunches
→ your obliques carve in and actually show
→ your hips get explosive again (this one hit different after surgery)
→ your shoulders stabilize and pop
→ your body stops leaking energy and starts moving like a weapon

This isn’t just a workout…
it’s how you build a body that looks athletic, moves athletic, and feels powerful again.

I had to earn this back step by step…
so if you’re skipping movements like this, you’re skipping the part that actually transforms you.

Most of you won’t commit to 80 reps a week… but the ones who do will look completely different in 30 days.

title:
My strength training routine as a runner:

Warmup 
Single leg bridges 2x10 each leg
Lateral lunges 20x alternating
Reverse lunges 20x each leg
Single leg RDL 2x8 each leg

Main set 
Goblet squats 4 x 8 - 95 lbs
Split squats 3 x 8 each leg - 90lbs
Single leg calf raise 3 x 15 - 90lbs
Push ups 3 x 12
(Done as circuit)

Capacity 
Hamstring bridge single leg 2 x 15 each leg
Side plank hip abduction 2 x 15 each leg
Dead bugs 2 x 30
Theraband Standing Fire Hydrant 2 x 15 each leg

Equipment: band loop, heavyish dumbbells, bench/chair for single leg ham bridges.

Remember to start light and progressively overload from there!

BACK

☑︎ Pike push-ups
☑︎ Handstand push-ups

ARMS

☑︎ Chin-ups (biceps)
☑︎ Dips (triceps)

CORE

☑︎ Hanging leg raises
☑︎ L-sits
☑︎ Planks

LEGS

☑︎ Squats

DEEP CORE

Master the basics first. 
Then add reps, range, and harder variations.

That’s how the physique changes (and you too)

Try this:

Pick 1 movement per category and train it 3x per week for 4 weeks.

Track reps and aim to beat last week

title:
Strength Training: Yes or No

The truth: muscle is not optional after 40. It’s how your body regulates blood sugar, protects your metabolism, and determines how well you age. Cardio matters. Walking matters. But resistance training is the lever most people are still underusing.

The skinny-fat concept is real, you can be at a “healthy” weight and still have the metabolic profile of someone at high risk. Muscle mass predicts long-term health better than body weight alone.
And no, lifting will not make women bulky. Bulk requires surplus calories and deliberate effort over a long time. What most women actually get is leaner, stronger, and far more metabolically resilient.

Start somewhere. Add resistance. Stay consistent.

Drop a ✅ if you’re already lifting

#strengthtraining #muscleafter40 #metabolichealth #skinnyfat #womenshealth

Core workout of the day! 99% of people are leaking power… and don’t even know it.

SHARE and save this for your workout today!

It’s why you feel tight… weak… or stuck no matter how much you train.

Not because you’re out of shape…
but because your core can’t control and transfer force.

I had to relearn this after double hip replacement…
but this applies to everyone.

If your core isn’t doing its job…
everything else suffers.

That’s why these kneeling flows matter…

They teach your body to:
• Lock in → then move
• Transfer power without leaking it
• Create strength that actually shows up in real life

This is what you’ll notice:

• You move smoother and feel more in control
• Your waist tightens while your core gets stronger
• Less stress on your hips and low back
• More power in everything… workouts, sports, daily movement
• You stop feeling stiff and start feeling athletic again

This isn’t just about looking good…
it’s about moving the way your body was built to.

I didn’t fix this by doing more exercises…
I fixed it by doing the right ones.

Most people don’t need more work…
they need better movement.

title:
I love bodybuilding!

But if that was the ONLY thing I did, then I’d have some serious gaps in my training.

I much prefer a blend of functional training, power and plyo work, Olympic and powerlifting, and multi-planar athletic movement. 

I use bodybuilding in every session to bring up some weaker areas or work on aesthetics in a certain muscle group, but I keep my training balanced beyond that.

If you’re a bodybuilder, a bro lifter, or “optimal science based” lifter then you do you! But it’s not the only way to train!

title:
FOUNDATIONAL STRENGTH
These four things should be incorporated in every. single. persons training routine.

1️⃣ Grip strength 
2️⃣ Pulling Motion
3️⃣ Hip Hinge
4️⃣ Focus on concentric + Eccentric

I make sure to incorporate all four of these things in every clients’ training plan, no matter their goals. Why? It’s a great setup for strength but also long term health and improving health span. Always think of the future you when you’re in the gym - what are the things you’d still like to be able to do when you’re 75?

Real time workout. Just you and the movement.
Today it’s just two exercises in a combo. Before, between, and after the exercises — run in place with a dumbbell for 10 seconds.

Format:
*  Just 2 exercises
*  20 seconds work
*  10 seconds running in place

Weight:
* I use 4 kg dumbbells (about 9 lbs each)
* If it feels easy, you can increase the weight or add ankle weights
* If it feels too challenging, perform the exercises with bodyweight only

If you are looking to improve your running, plyometrics are a great addition! Plyometrics work the stretch-shortening cycle, and put simply, more spring means more force and a faster run!

1️⃣ Lateral hops x 20s each side
2️⃣ Front to back hops x 20s
3️⃣ Tuck Jumps x 20s
4️⃣ Plyo lunge x 20s
5️⃣ Hinge to Hop x 20s each side
✅ Rest for 20s between movements
✅ Complete 3 rounds

Save this to make to you a better runner!

title:
More info 👇

One of the biggest mistakes I see is runners trying to swing their arms forwards and backwards aggressively without realising what it’s doing to the rest of the body.

Your right and left side are connected 🤯

So when your arm reaches too far out in front of you, your opposite leg often starts overstriding with it.

That means:

❌ More braking forces
❌ Less efficiency
❌ Higher injury risk

Overstriding is one of the most common issues I see in injured runners.

The arm swing should support your stride, not fight against it.

Think:
✅ Smoothly backwards
✅ Like a string is pulling it back
✅ Level with the ground at slow paces

Not:
❌ aggressive reaching forwards

Share this with a runner who needs to see it ✉️

Visit my bio for coaching 🔥 

#running #runner #run

title:
mental tricks to help you run for longer when you want to stop because running is a MENTAL game 🧠⭐️🏃🏻‍♀️👇🏼

1️⃣ choose a mantra to repeat to keep you focused!!
⭐️ ‘strong and steady’ or ‘one more step’ or ‘empty the tank’

2️⃣ break the run into smaller chunks!! 
⭐️ instead of thinking “I’ve got 10km left” focus only on finishing the next km or split it into 2 park runs!

3️⃣ focus on your form or anything that still feels good!! 
⭐️ legs feeling heavy, but breathing is ok? focus on breathing!
⭐️ feeling uncomfortable? focus on relaxing your shoulders & running light on your feet!

4️⃣ visualise the end or finish line!!
⭐️ think about how happy you will feel when you achieve it who you will see at the end or what treat you will get after! coffee? pastry?

5️⃣ quickly reframe any negative thought!!
⭐️ ”I’m slowing down” ➡️ “at least I’m not stopping”
⭐️ “this hurts a lot” ➡️ “this is where I improve”
⭐️ “I’m not good at running” to “I’m better than I was before”

6️⃣ try mental games to take your mind off of running!!
⭐️ count your steps up to 20 or 30 and then start again!
⭐️ count how my cars you see in a certain colour! challenge a friend - first to spot 10 cars in their colour!

#runner #runtok #runningtips #runwithme

title:
The mistake slowing most runners down ⚠️

Master this one technique shift and your running will instantly feel more efficient.

🏃‍♂️ DON’T: Bend at the waist

✅ DO: Lean forward from your ankles

When you hinge at the waist, your centre of mass stays behind your feet. Gravity can’t help! You have to muscle every stride.

But when you keep your posture tall and lean slightly from the ankles, gravity starts doing the work for you. It’s like free energy.

🎈 Think: “Balloon lifts your head, bungee cord pulls your chest forward.”

You’ll run smoother, faster and feel way less impact.

🎥 Save this tip
💬 Comment “FYS” if you’re ready to change up your running today 🔥

title:
If you want to run faster, the research is pretty clear on what actually works.

48 competitive endurance athletes were split into 4 groups for 9 weeks: high volume easy running, threshold intervals, HIIT, and polarized training. The polarized group — mostly easy running + 2 hard sessions per week at 90% max HR — beat every other group on every single metric. VO2 max up 11.7%. Time to exhaustion up 17.4%. (PMID: 24550842)

A second study of 30 runners compared polarized training against threshold-dominant training over 10 weeks. Polarized group improved 10K performance by 5.0% vs 3.5%. (PMID: 23752040)

Go easier on easy days. And go very hard on hard days. That's where the adaptation is.

Most runners live in the middle. That's the problem.

📚 Full studies: PMID 24550842 | PMID 23752040

title:
Proper Running Footstrike - 3 Steps to Improve! 💯

Follow 👉 @_strongbodies for daily pain relief tips! 📚

⁣There are three different running foot strike patterns: heel strike, mid-foot strike and fore-foot strike.⁣
⁣
It only takes a few seconds to transform a heel strike to a mid-foot strike during drills. However, the actual transformation can take months because of the physical adaptation time it takes for your muscles, tendons, bones, and nerves to “learn”⁣ the new movement pattern 💪⁣
⁣
But in some “heel-strike-cases” (if you have pain while running or you are often injured) it’s beneficial and worth the work to transform the footing‼️⁣
⁣
When runners move along in a heel-striking mode, every bit of ground contact causes impact forces to pass through the heel and up the leg. The knees and hips are left to carry out a higher level of work to withstand, control and react to these rapidly applied forces. Additionally, the shin muscles become highly stressed 🚨⁣
⁣
However, the force patterns change dramatically with mid-foot strikes. Every impact immediately distributes forces throughout the foot and ankle, resulting in less stress for the body (less injuries!).⁣
⁣
Try these exercises shown in the reel to do the first steps into a more efficient running form 🔥💯🔥⁣

title:
Most beginners think they have to run a certain way… 

but truth is:

Everyone’s running style is a little different

Your body, structure, and experience all play a role

The 3 foot strikes 👣 

1️⃣ Heel strike: heel lands first

Feels natural for beginners 

The main issue is usually overstriding which could lead to shin splints 

2️⃣ Midfoot strike: whole foot lands together

Smooth, balanced, controlled

Often more efficient for most runners

3️⃣Forefoot strike: front of foot lands first

Great for speed

More stress on calves/Achilles over long runs

So what’s best?

There’s no universal “best”

The goal is to run smooth, comfortable, and pain-free

I personally prefer midfoot striking because:

It feels the most efficient

The landing is softer and smoother

The impact is spread more evenly through the legs instead of hitting one area hard

But that doesn’t mean you have to force it

Don’t overthink your foot strike

Focus on shorter, quicker steps

Let your body naturally adjust over time

If it feels smooth and pain-free -> you’re doing it right

Hope this helps 🙌

title:
Do these BEFORE & AFTER your run to feel stronger and recover faster! 🏃‍♀️💯

Before your run (Dynamic warm-up):
Activate your muscles + get the blood flowing!
✨ Hamstring Sweeps
✨ Ankling
✨ Squats
✨ Butt Kicks
✨ Hip CARs
✨ Reverse Lunges + Calf Raise
👉 45 sec each drill

After your run (Static stretches):
Cool down, recover + improve flexibility!
✨ Single-leg Hamstring Stretch
✨ Calf Stretch
✨ Deep Squat Hold
✨ Single-leg Quad Stretch
✨ Standing Glute Stretch
✨ Lunge Stretch
👉 Hold 1 min each stretch

💡 Pro tip: Skipping warm-ups = higher risk of injury. Skipping cool-downs = stiffer muscles tomorrow. Don’t skip either!

🏃🏽‍♀️Do it to become quicker off the ground so running feels easier and you can go faster. Ankling is a simple drill that teaches your feet to touch the ground quickly and bounce back up fast.

Technical cues:
* Small, quick steps close to the ground
* Feet land under your hips 
* Toes up before contact
* Contact the ground with the ball of your foot 
* Stay tall with an engaged core

With running becoming more popular, many people skip the basics. But better mechanics make running feel easier, reduce the risk of injury, and ultimately make you faster.

🍗 Creamy Ranch Chicken Bake
Ingredients
• 5-6 chicken breasts
• 1 packet ranch seasoning
• 2 blocks cream cheese (softened)
• ½ cup shredded cheddar
• Optional: bacon bits or chopped green onion
Instructions
1. Heat oven to 400°F.
2. Lay chicken in a baking dish & season with salt, pepper, garlic powder, garlic salt 
3. Mix ranch seasoning + cream cheese + cheddar + bacon bits in a bowl.
4. Spread mixture over chicken.

Dumb Dinners, Episode 24: Feta Melt Pasta Bake

What you’ll need:
12 oz short pasta (rigatoni or penne)
3 cups chicken broth
1 lb pre-cooked Italian sausage, sliced or crumbled
12 oz roasted red peppers, drained + roughly chopped
1 (8 oz) block feta
3 tbsp olive oil
1 tsp garlic powder
1/2 tsp salt
1/2 tsp black pepper
1/2 tsp Italian seasoning
1/4–1/3 cup heavy cream
Fresh basil to finish

How to make it:
Preheat oven to 400°F
Add pasta, broth, olive oil, and seasonings to a 9x13 dish. Stir to combine.
Stir in sausage and roasted red peppers
Place feta block in the center. Don’t stir.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 35–40 min until pasta is tender
Remove from oven, stir in heavy cream, and break up the feta until creamy
Stir in fresh basil before serving

title:
Creamy Pesto Chicken Pasta Bake ✨ My most viral recipe of 2024! 

What a year it’s been. I’m truly so grateful for all the love and support you’ve shown me this year. Cheers to a delicious 2025! 

Here’s how to make it:

1lb pasta of choice
1/2 cup sun-dried tomatoes + oil
1lb chicken
1 tbsp butter
1/2 yellow onion, diced
Salt and pepper, to taste 1 tsp red pepper flakes (to taste)
1 tsp smoked paprika (to taste)
1 tsp oregano (to taste)
6-8 cloves of garlic, minced (to taste)
2 cups heavy cream (room temp)
1-2 cups cooked broccoli 
2 handfuls spinach
6-8 oz freshly shredded parmesan cheese (divided)
8 oz freshly shredded mozzarella (divided)
1/2 cup pesto, to taste (I recommend Costco brand)
Parsley to garnish 
1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Place the cream on the counter to come to room temp.
2. Boil your noodles in salted water a few minutes less than package instructions (al dente). Drain and set aside. 
3. In a large oven-safe saucepan or dutch oven, heat 1 tbsp of sun-dried tomato oil over medium heat. Cook the chicken until it's no longer pink, then remove it from the pan and set it aside. Let it rest for a few minutes before cutting into bite-sized pieces.
4. In the same pan, melt the butter and add salt, pepper, red pepper, paprika, and oregano. Stir to toast, then toss in the onion and sauté for about 4 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.
5. Turn heat to low, pour in the heavy cream and stir. Let it simmer for a couple of minutes to thicken slightly.
6. Add half of the parmesan and 1 cup of mozzarella cheese,  stir until the cheese is melted.
7. Stir in the sun-dried tomatoes, cooked broccoli, spinach, chicken, cooked pasta, and pesto.
8. Top with the remaining mozzarella and parmesan cheese. 
9. Bake at 350°F for 15 minutes, then broil for another 5 minutes, or until the top is golden and bubbly.
10. Sprinkle with fresh parsley, a little more parmesan, and enjoy!

title:
It's #trendingtuesday and @Alexa Santos is making Bala Baiana 🥥 These coconut bon bons are a Brazilian dessert you can make with just a few simple ingredients! IB @KITCHENTOOL & @Sarah Kraffty 

Recipe details below.

INGREDIENTS:
1 tablespoon butter
1 (14 ounce) can sweetened condensed milk
2/3 cup sweetened coconut flakes
1 cup granulated sugar
1/2 cup water
1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar

RECIPE:
1. Melt butter in a large pan over medium heat. Pour in the sweetened condensed milk and coconut flakes. Stir to mix, then cook, stirring occasionally, about 7 minutes. The mixture should form almost into a dough-like texture that easily pulls away from the pan.
2. Move the mixture into a bowl, cover, and place into the fridge to cool.
3. Line a baking sheet with parchment. Grease your hands, and roll the coconut mixture into ping pong sized balls. Place onto the parchment, then stick a toothpick into each one.
4. Heat a large pan over medium high. Pour in the sugar, water, and vinegar. Bring to a boil and cook for about 10 minutes, or until the mixture is amber colored.
5. Working quickly and carefully, use the toothpicks to dip each ball into the sugar mixture. Try to evenly coat them, then set each one back on the parchment.
6. Let cool, then enjoy! Store in the fridge for a few days.

Dinner in 10 minutes? 🍋

This Easy lemon chicken recipe (Pollo al Limone) comes together in about 10 minutes, so there’s really no excuse not to have a great tasting weeknight dinner. Bright lemon, butter, and parsley make the perfect quick sauce! One of those recipes you’ll make on repeat.

Ingredients:
1 lb chicken breast filets
2 lemons
1/2 cup white wine
1 knob butter
Olive oil
Salt & pepper
Fresh parsley
Flour (for dredging)

Directions:
1. Lightly flour the chicken breast filets.
2. Sauté in olive oil over medium heat until lightly golden on both sides. Season with salt and pepper.
3. Add the white wine, lemon peel from one lemon, lemon zest from the other, and the juice of both lemons.
4. Add the butter and parsley.
5. Cook on low for a few minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce slightly thickens.

Calories & Macros 📊

- 500g lean ground beef (5% fat or less)

- 10g diced chilli (optional for heat - sub with 1/2 tsp cayenne)

- 1 tsp smoked paprika

Potato Pocket Dough

Storage & Heating ♨️
- Once cooled wrap in foil and store in the fridge or freezer
- To reheat from the fridge, unwrap from the foil and microwave for 1-2 minutes. toast in the pan for a couple minutes to get crispy again

Dip or drizzle—done!

Chicken Breast
Cream Cheese

Jalapeños 
Bacon
Colby Jack Cheese

Paprika

Black Pepper
Garlic Powder
Ranch Seasoning
Onion Powder

Instructions:

Preheat your oven to 350°F.

Cut your chicken into bite-sized pieces and add them to a 7x11 baking dish.

Season the chicken with onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper, seasoned salt, and paprika. Mix well to ensure everything is evenly coated.

In a separate bowl, add one block of softened cream cheese and season with garlic powder and pepper.

Add a spoonful of sour cream, one diced jalapeño, 3 pieces of crumbled bacon, a handful of Colby Jack cheese, and one packet of ranch seasoning. Mix until well combined.

Spread the mixture evenly over the chicken. Top with additional cheese and bacon.

Bake for 45 minutes, or until the chicken is fully cooked and the top is hot and bubbly.

Enjoy!🤍👩🏼‍🍳

title:
Honey Garlic Chicken! 🍯 🧄  Sticky, sweet, garlicky, and comes together so easy… this one’s a weeknight winner every time!!

@Courtney Cook made my recipe the other day and it made me want it all over again!! Serve it over rice with a veggie, so good y’all. 

Ingredients:
 • 3 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
 • ½ tbsp garlic salt
 • 1 tbsp black pepper
 • ¼ cup cornstarch (plus a little extra if you want more crunch)
 • 2–3 tbsp vegetable oil (for frying)

Sauce:
 • ½ cup honey
 • ¼ cup soy sauce
 • 1 tbsp ginger paste
 • 2–3 tbsp minced garlic

To Finish:
 • Sesame seeds
 • Green onions, sliced

⸻

Instructions:
 1. Season the chicken
In a large bowl, add chicken, garlic salt, black pepper, and cornstarch. Toss until everything is well coated. (Add a little extra cornstarch if you want it extra crispy.)
 2. Cook the chicken
Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add chicken in batches and cook until browned on both sides with a light crust. Don’t overcrowd the pan. Remove and set aside.
 3. Make the sauce
Add all the cooked chicken back to the skillet. Pour in honey, soy sauce, ginger paste, and minced garlic. Toss to coat.
 4. Simmer
Let it simmer for a few minutes until the sauce thickens and gets sticky, coating all the chicken.
 5. Finish & serve
Top with sesame seeds and green onions. Serve over white rice with your favorite veggie.
 #yum #easyrecipe #chicken

title:
A Simple Recipe for French Fries
To make classic French fries, first peel and cut 2-3 large russet potatoes into even batons about 1/2 cm thick. Soak them in cold water for 30 minutes to remove excess starch, then pat them completely dry with a kitchen towel. Heat a pot of oil to 325°F (160°C) and fry the potatoes in batches for 4-5 minutes until soft but not colored; this is the first fry. Remove and drain on paper towels. Now, increase the oil temperature to 375°F (190°C). Fry the potatoes for a second time for 2-3 minutes until they are golden brown and crispy. Drain immediately, season generously with salt, and serve hot.

title:
Red curry cabbage cups 🥬 the most satisfying dinner with minimal prep 

1 large green cabbage

Chicken filling:
500 g chicken breast mince
2 tbsp red curry paste
1/2-3/4 cup panko crumbs
1 spring onion, finely chopped
1/3 cup coriander, chopped
1/2 tbsp ginger, grated 
1 tbsp brown sugar
1 tsp fish sauce
Juice and zest of 1 lime
1 egg

Red curry sauce: 
2 tbsp red curry paste
400 ml coconut milk
1 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp rice wine vinegar

Method
	1.	Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Add whole cabbage and boil for a few minutes until outer leaves soften.
	2.	Carefully peel off 4-5 large leaves. Trim off thick stalks.
	3.	Place one cabbage leaf into a small bowl to form a cup.
	4.	In a bowl, mix all chicken filling ingredients until just combined.
	5.	Spoon filling into cabbage cups and gently press to hold shape.
	6.	Arrange cabbage cups snugly in an ovenproof pan.
	7.	Whisk all red curry sauce ingredients and pour over cabbage cups.
	8.	Bake at 180C for 45 minutes until cooked through and bubbling.
	9.	Spoon sauce over to serve.
#cabbage #easydinner #healthy

title:
🔥 Cajun Chicken Pasta – One Bite and You’re Hooked!

Ingredients:

✅ For the Chicken:

•2 chicken breast fillets
•2 tbsp olive oil

Cajun seasoning:

•1 tsp paprika (sweet or smoked)
•½ tsp garlic powder
•½ tsp onion powder
•½ tsp oregano
•½ tsp thyme
•½ tsp black pepper
•½ tsp cayenne pepper (to taste)
•½ tsp salt

✅ For the Sauce:
•1 tbsp butter
•1 small onion, diced
•1 red bell pepper, diced
•250 ml heavy cream
•½ tsp bouillon powder (chicken broth)
•1 tsp Cajun seasoning
•1 handful fresh spinach
•50 g Parmesan cheese, grated
•50 g Mozzarella cheese, grated
•250 g pasta 

✅ For Garnishing:
•Chili powder
•Fresh parsley

🥩 Preparing & Cooking the Chicken:

1. Rub the chicken breasts with olive oil and generously season with Cajun seasoning.

2. Sear in a pan over medium-high heat for about 2–3 minutes per side until a nice crust forms.

3. Remove the chicken from the pan and place it on a baking sheet.

4. Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (356°F) for about 12–15 minutes, until it reaches an internal temperature of 74°C (165°F).

5. Remove from the oven and let it rest for a few minutes.

🥣 Making the Creamy Cajun Sauce:
1. In the same pan, melt 1 tbsp butter.
2. Sauté the onions & bell pepper until softened.
3. Deglaze with heavy cream and stir in the bouillon powder.
4. Add Cajun seasoning & spinach and let it simmer briefly.
5. Stir in Parmesan & Mozzarella until the sauce becomes creamy.
6. Add the cooked pasta to the sauce and mix well.

🍗 Final Touch
Garnish with chili powder & fresh parsley.

title:
Creamy Chipotle Chicken & Potatoes🍗🍟🧀

One of the most indulgent meal prep recipes, so creamy, rich in flavour and packed with protein. Using a sheet pan is a game changer for batch cooking🔥

Macros Per Serving (6 Total)

548 Calories | 51g Protein | 52g Carbs | 17g Fat

Ingredients (Makes 6 Servings)

Chipotle Chicken Marinade
- 1200g Raw Boneless Chicken Thighs, trim excess fat
- 2.5 Tsp Salt
- 3 Tsp Parsley
- 3 Tsp Garlic Powder
- 3 Tsp Smoked Paprika
- 2.5 Tsp Cumin
- 3 Tsp Onion Powder
- 100g Chipotle Paste
- 1 and 1/2 Limes, juiced
- 30g or 6 Tsp Olive Oil
Let this marinate overnight if possible, way more flavor!

Crispy Seasoned Potatoes
- 1300g Raw Yellow Potatoes, cubed
- 2.5 Tsp Garlic Powder
- 3 Tsp Italian Herbs
- 3 Tsp Smoked Paprika
- 2.5 Tsp Onion Powder
- Avocado Cooking Spray, heavy pass

Creamy Chipotle Sauce
- 20g Light Butter
- 150-200g Red Onion, finely chopped
- 1.5 Tsp Salt
- 2 Tsp Italian Herbs
- 60-80g Chipotle Paste (depends how spicy you want it)
- 400g Light Evaporated Milk
- 110g Light Cream Cheese
- Freshly Chopped Parsley, garnish

👨‍🍳 Cooking Instructions

1. Trim excess fat from chicken thighs. Add seasonings, chipotle paste, lime juice, and olive oil. Mix well and marinate.
2. Heat a large pan on low, add butter and chopped red onion. Cook for 5-7 mins until softened and lightly browned. Add seasonings and chipotle paste, mix, and cook for another 5 mins until caramelised.
3. Keep the heat low, add evaporated milk and cream cheese. Stir continuously until smooth, rich, and creamy.
4. Cube up potatoes, add seasoning and cooking spray, then mix well. Spread on a lined sheet pan and roast at 200C / 390F for 25 mins until golden and crispy. Season with salt, then fold into the sauce with fresh parsley until fully coated.
5. Spread marinated chicken on sheet pan, oven bake 25 mins 200C / 390F until golden and juicy. Cut into cubes, serve with creamy potatoes and ENJOY!

This week’s meal prep:

🍎 Apple Pie Overnight Oats (4 servings)

Ingredients (for all 4 containers):

* 2 cups rolled oats
* 2 tbsp chia seeds
* 2 cups Kirkland oat milk
* 2 Gala apples, diced
* Cinnamon
* 1 tsp vanilla extract
* Pinch of salt
* 2 Ratio protein yogurts (25g protein each)

⸻

Instructions (PER CONTAINER)

1. Add into each meal prep container:
    * 1/2 cup rolled oats
    * 1/2 tbsp chia seeds
    * 1/2 cup oat milk
    * pinch cinnamon
    * splash vanilla
    * pinch salt
2. Stir everything directly inside the container.
3. Cook apples in a pan with cinnamon for 4–5 minutes until soft and glossy.
4. Layer in each container:
    * oat mixture (bottom)
    * 1/2 Ratio yogurt (middle layer)
    * cooked cinnamon apples (top)
5. Refrigerate overnight.

Macros (per serving):

* ~410–470 calories
* ~24–30g protein
* ~55–65g carbs
* ~8–11g fat

⸻

🌶️ High-Protein Buffalo Chicken Dip (4 servings)

Ingredients:

* 1 lb shredded chicken
* 1/2 cup Good Culture cottage cheese
* 1/2 cup fat-free Fage Greek yogurt
* 1/3–1/2 cup Frank’s cayenne pepper sauce
* 1–1.5 cups low-moisture mozzarella
* Garlic powder, onion powder, pepper
* Green onions (for topping)

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 375°F.
2. Blend cottage cheese + Greek yogurt + hot sauce until smooth.
3. Mix with shredded chicken + seasonings.
4. Stir in half the mozzarella.
5. Transfer to baking dish and top with remaining mozzarella.
6. Bake 20–25 minutes (broil 1–2 min for cheese pull).
7. Top with green onions.

Macros (per serving):

* ~290–350 calories
* ~36–43g protein
* ~3–6g carbs
* ~10–13g fat

⸻

🦐 Lemon Shrimp Orzo (4 servings)

Ingredients:

* 1 lb shrimp
* 1 cup dry orzo
* 1 bunch asparagus, chopped
* 2 cups bone broth
* 1/2 cup fat-free Fage Greek yogurt
* 1 tbsp olive oil
* Garlic, salt, pepper
* Lemon juice + zest
* Parsley (garnish)
* Shredded Parmesan (topping)

Instructions:

1. Cook shrimp in olive oil until pink, then remove.
2. Sauté garlic + asparagus in same pan.
3. Add orzo and toast for 1 minute.
4. Pour in bone broth and simmer 8–10 minutes until tender.
5. Lower heat and stir in Greek yogurt + lemon juice.
6. Add shrimp back in.
7. Top with Parmesan + parsley.

Macros (per serving):

* ~430–500 calories
* ~34–40g protein
* ~38–45g carbs
* ~10–14g fat

Crispy Garlic Parmesan Chicken Wraps🍗🧀🌯

The flavours are absolutely phenomenal, one of the best wraps made using a sheet pan. Low effort, minimal cleanup and incredibly delicious🔥 Great to serve for large groups/gatherings at home

Macros Per Wrap (10 Total)

423 Calories | 41g Protein | 25g Carbs | 18g Fat

Ingredients (Makes 10 Wraps)

Garlic Parmesan Chicken
- 600g Raw Boneless Skinless Chicken Thighs, cut into cubes
- 600g Raw Chicken Breast, cut into cubes
- 2.5 Tsp Salt
- 2 Tsp Chilli Flakes
- 3 Tsp Parsley
- 4 Tsp Italian Herbs
- 3 Tsp Paprika
- 4 Tsp Garlic Granules or Powder
- 200g Grated Parmesan
- 6 Tsp Olive Oil
- Avocado Cooking Spray (use before baking)

Garlic Pamesan Creamy Sauce
- 350g Light Evaporated Milk
- 2 Tsp Italian Herbs
- 1 Tsp Garlic Powder
- 1 Tsp Paprika
- 80g Grated Parmesan
- 100g Light Cream Cheese
- 15g Light Butter

Wraps & Filling
- 10 Low Carb Wraps (Brand: Mission)
- Shredded Lettuce
- Chopped Tomatoes
- Chopped Onions

👨‍🍳 Cooking Instructions

1. Slice chicken breast and thighs into cubes. Add seasonings with grated parmesan cheese and drizzle of olive oil. Mix until well coated.
2. In a pan on low heat, add light butter with seasonings. Toast for a minute before adding evaporated milk, extra Parmesan and cream cheese. Stir till smooth and creamy.
3. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper, spread marinated chicken evenly (do not overcrowd), add light layer of cooking spray then bake in a preheated oven for 20-22 mins at 200C until crispy.
4. While chicken is still hot, add extra parmesan and parsley. Mix well until coated and extra cheesy.
5. Assemble the wraps with shredded lettuce, onion, tomato, crispy chicken and sauce. ENJOY!

Storage and Reheating Tips
- Store chicken and creamy sauce in separate containers in the fridge.
- When ready to eat, just warm up chicken in oven/air fryer for 4-5 mins 180C / 370F. Warm up sauce in a pan, serve on a wrap with fresh lettuce and enjoy

title:
Crispy Sweetcorn Chipotle Chicken Salad 🌽🥗 

Trust me when I say this crispy sweetcorn chipotle chicken salad is about to become your new obsession!! 😍 It’s crunchy, fresh, smoky, packed with flavour and makes the perfect high protein meal prep for the week. Save for later☝🏼

•452 kcals (not including tortilla chips)
•44g PRO, 25g CHO, 18g FAT

Serves 1:
-100g of uncooked chicken breast
-1 tsp of paprika
-1/2 tsp of garlic granules
-Oil spray
-80g of drained sweetcorn
-Salt/pepper
-1/4 of a large cucumber, finely diced
-1/2-1 red onion, finely diced
-Handful of fresh parsley and/or coriander, chopped 
-30g of feta cheese, crumbled 
-2 tbsp of grated parmesan 
-Tortilla chips, to serve (optional & not included in calories)
Dressing:
-100g of 0% Greek yoghurt
-1 tsp of olive oil
-1 tsp of chipotle paste
-Squeeze of lemon juice
-Salt/pepper

Method:
1. Season chicken with paprika and garlic granules. Spray with oil and air fry or cook in the oven at 180°C for 15-20 minutes. Chop into chunks once cooked and cooled. 
2. Place corn in a lined air fryer, season with salt and pepper. Spray with oil and air fry at 180°C for 15-20 minutes until charred and crispy. 
3. Remove seeds from the cucumber and finely dice along with red onion and parsley. 
4. For the dressing, mix all the ingredients together.
5. Add the cucumber, red onion, chicken, parsley, half of the feta cheese, 1 tbsp of parmesan, half of the crispy corn and the dressing. Toss together.
6. Serve in a bowl, top with the remaining feta, corn and 1 tbsp of parmesan. Enjoy on it’s own or with some tortilla chips on the side.

Enjoy!

INGREDIENTS
For Chicken

• ½ tsp each: chili powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder

• 1-3 Tbsp water (as needed to thin it out)

For Street Corn
• 3 c corn, cooked

• ¼ c red onion, chopped
• ¼ c cilantro, chopped
• ¼ c cotija cheese

For Cilantro Lime Rice
• 1 c jasmine rice, uncooked
• 1 Tbsp extra virgin olive oil
• ½ c cilantro, chopped
• 2 Tbsp lime juice
• ½ tsp each: garlic powder, kosher salt
• ¼ tsp black pepper

For Assembling (opt)
• romaine 
• avo
• tomatoes

DIRECTIONS
1. Prep chicken: Cut chicken into cubes. Coat in 1 Tbsp olive oil + seasonings. Set aside to let marinade.

title:
This week’s menu👩‍🍳: overnight oats, muffins, buffalo chicken wraps, and Mexican beef bowls.
Not something I do every week, but it makes life so much easier when I do. 
All supplements and protein powders used are from @Naked Harvest Supplements - plus you can use my code LAURENJ for a cheeky discount 😉.
-
RECIPES:
Banana Choc Muffins 🍌 :
In a large bowl, mash 2 ripe bananas and mix with 2 eggs, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, 2 tablespoons sugar-free maple syrup (or regular maple/honey), and ½ cup vanilla YoPro (protein yogurt).
To the same bowl, add 2 tablespoons monk fruit sweetener (or sweetener of choice), ½ cup Naked Harvest Chocolate Malt Thrive Plant Protein, ½ cup self-raising flour, 2 tablespoons cocoa powder, and a pinch of pink salt, then fold everything together until just combined.
Fold in ⅔ cup NoShu chocolate chips (I used a mix of dark and white), reserving some to sprinkle on top.
Divide mixture into muffin trays lined with patty pans (makes 6 jumbo or 12 small muffins).
Bake at 170°C for 25–30 minutes, or until a skewer comes out clean.
Let cool for 15 minutes. Serve warm. Store in an airtight container in the fridge and reheat in the microwave when ready to eat.

Macros per serve (based on 6 jumbo muffins): ~215 kcal | 12g protein | 18g carbs | 8g fats

Apple Cinnamon Overnight Oats 🍎 :
Add 2 chopped apples, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, 1 teaspoon sugar-free maple syrup, ¼ cup water, a squeeze of lemon juice, and 1 teaspoon corn flour to a small saucepan.
Stew over medium heat until thickened and the apples are soft.
Remove from heat and let the apple mixture cool completely.
In a jar or bowl, combine ½ cup oats, 1 tablespoon chia seeds, 25g Naked Harvest vanilla or caramel protein powder, and a dash of cinnamon.
Add 1 tablespoon sugar-free maple syrup and ¼ cup water, then stir until smooth and combined.
Let oats sit in the fridge for 15 minutes.
Top with ¼ of the stewed apple mixture, a dollop (approx. 2 tablespoons) of vanilla YoPro, a sprinkle of cinnamon, and a drizzle of honey.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before eating (preferably overnight).
Macros per serve: ~360 kcal | 25g protein | 35g carbs | 10g fat

Buffalo Chicken Mix 🌯:
Add 300g roasted shredded chicken, 200g cottage cheese, 3 diced celery sticks, and 1 large diced dill pickle to a large bowl.
Add a sprinkle of fresh or dried dill, 80g light mayo, 1 tablespoon pickle juice, seasoning of choice, and ½ packet of Mingle Buffalo Chicken seasoning.
Mix everything together until well combined and creamy.
Serve as a dip, in a wrap, sandwich, or salad.
Makes 3–4 serves. Store in the fridge in an airtight container.
Macros per serve (based on 4 serves): ~210 kcal | 27g protein | 3g carbs | 10g fat

Mexican-Style Beef Mince 🫘:
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large non-stick pan and cook 1 diced onion with 1 tablespoon minced garlic.
Add 1 grated carrot and 1 grated zucchini, then cook until softened.
Add 500g lean beef mince and brown thoroughly.
Stir in 400g canned crushed tomatoes, 300g canned corn, 400g Mexican-style bean mix, 1 packet Mingle taco seasoning, and 2 tablespoons Mingle BBQ sauce.
Let the mixture simmer on medium heat until thickened.
Allow to cool completely before portioning.
Serve with rice and vegetables of choice.
Macros per serve (1/5 of beef mix only): ~320 kcal | 28g protein | 18g carbs | 16g fat

title:
✅ HEALTHY LUNCH IDEA, PART 19

I’ve lost 150+lbs and this is one of my favorite healthy meal prep options. It’s keeps me insanely full with the slow digesting carbs, protein, health fats, and fiber. Plus the healthier homemade sugar free hot honey sauce is SO good.

If you are watching carbs, feel free to sub spaghetti squash, eggplant, or even zucchini instead of butternut squash.

Here is how I made it (makes 4 servings)

1.Finely dice 1 medium butternut squash. You’ll want this finely diced so it cooks faster. Drizzle with 1 tsp olive oil, season with salt, pepper, 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp smoked paprika, and 1 tsp Chile lime seasoning (or tajin). Add to a tray, pop in the oven for 27-30 mins at 400F.

2.Do the same thing with another lower sugar, high fiber veggie. I used 2 cups of broccoli florets . Same thing - drizzle with olive oil, season with salt, pepper, and the same spices. Pop in the oven until nice and crispy.

3.Cook 1 lb lean ground beef (I used 93/7)) on medium high heat in 1 tsp olive oil. Season your beef with salt, pepper, 1 tbsp onion powder, 1 tbsp garlic powder, 1 tbsp oregano, 1.5 tbsp smoked paprika, and 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper. Use a spoon or a spatula to mince it down to small pieces. I like to get meat browned really well, almost crispy, so this should take about 15-17 mins.

4.When your butternut squash and broccoli are roasted, divide it up in to 4 different serving bowls or meal prep containers. Add 4oz of the seasoned beef, a quarter of an avocado cubed, 3tbsp thick greek yogurt, and any sauce you like. I like using a low sugar hot honey sauce here (step 5 below) but you can use a bottled hot honey, or any sauce you like.

5.For the sugar free hot honey sauce, in a small pan over low heat, stir together 5 tbsp sugar-free (or regular) honey, 2 tbsp sriracha, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and 1/2 to 1 tsp chili flakes for about a minute. I used about 2 tbsp of sauce for each.

This is a great healthy lunch recipe, and perfect for a healthy meal prep. Per serving 510 cals, 30g prot, 18 net carbs.

24 tortillas
1-2 lbs of sausage

3 green peppers
1 white onion

title:
High Protein Frozen Burritos are the Ultimate Meal Prep

Meal prepping and freezing high protein burritos changed the game for me - and was actually the first “meal prep” content I ever made

I had honestly never meal prepped until I realized just how convenient having easy, high protein meals stocked in my freezer was. It made my life SO MUCH easier on days I didn’t feel like cooking

Since I started posting frozen burrito recipes, I’ve received thousands of DMs showing your freezers stocked with 10, 20, 30 and even 100+ of my high protein burritos at a time

If you’re looking to enter the burrito meal prep game, here are my top tips👇

Freeze Your Burritos
- Storing frozen keeps burritos tasting their best, and allows them to last for months. It allows you to prep in huge bulk (think 20-30 burritos/meals at at time) without worrying about them going bad/going uneaten
- Wrap individually and freeze, or place burritos on a sheet pan and toss in the freezer uncovered (“flash freeze”) and then add to a gallon sized bag. Flash freezing first keeps them from sticking together while freezing

Reheat Method
 - Remove your burrito straight from the freezer, wrap in a paper towel, microwave for 1.5-2 minutes to thaw (flip halfway) - the goal is to get the interior softened but not hot. Next, air fry (I usually do 375 degrees for 6-7 minutes), or pan fry until crispy. Your burritos will come out perfectly crisp (not soggy) and taste as good, if not better, than fresh

Slowly Stockpile
- You don’t need to spend hours and hours prepping - start by making 1-2 of my recipes a week (which will usually yield 20-30 burritos/meals). Repeat weekly, rotating recipes based on preference, and you’ll slowly build a huge stockpile of frozen meals. The concept is to be in a “meal prep surplus” - cooking more than you eat each week, until you eventually have enough meals to last for months

Make a Low Calorie Side Sauce
- I like to make simple, high protein yogurt sauces as a pairing. Low fat greek yogurt (and Skyr) taste nearly identical to sour cream - and can also add an additional 10+ grams of protein to your meal for minimal calories. Try mixing plain yogurt or Skyr with your favorite hot sauce for a delicious dipping sauce. If you’re hesitant, start with full-fat greek yogurt (5%) which still has a great protein-to-calorie ratio and tastes incredible

Cool the Filling Before Rolling
- When I prep burritos in bulk, I tend to just mix everything together to create a “filling” instead of adding each ingredient separately. After creating the filling, I like to place it in the fridge/freezer for 15-20 minutes so it can thicken - and it makes rolling burritos perfectly completely effortless

If you’re looking for recipe ideas - I have an entire chapter in my meal prep cookbook dedicated to high protein frozen burrito preps, and tons of recipes on my feed

title:
📌Save For: How To Lego Meal Prep

👍Like this post and comment ‘Meal Plan’ for the recipes!

The way I meal prep may have just changed for good when I discovered the concept of lego meals - which blew my mind (inspired by @little.vegan.eats!). This is the perfect solution for families with different meal preferences or for those that like variety throughout the week but still want to meal plan. Also an amazing way to save money and reduce waste.

Basically you make components of the meals and freeze them in individual containers. You can then mix and match meal ingredients based on your preference. Once you are ready to eat, defrost in the microwave and add flavour enhancers like hummus, guacamole or additional herbs and spices.

If you want to meal prep like this, I recommend starting with 3-4 veggies, 2-3 proteins and  1-2 starches. Save this post to steal this meal prep strategy. Have you ever meal prepped liked this?

I used @soupercubes molds for this prep!

For this meal prep I made:
- Sweet potato chili bowls (one with rice and carrots, one with sweet potatoes and green beans)
- Teriyaki tofu bowls (teriyaki tofu with rice, peppers and broccoli)
- Lentil Bolognese pasta ( with peppers)

I used the following ingredients:

PROTEINS:
- Teriyaki Tofu
- Lentil Bolognese
- Bean Chili
- Protein Pasta

VEGETABLES:
- Roasted Peppers
- Green Beans
- Broccoli
- Carrots

STARCHES:
- Roasted Sweet Potatoes Cubes
- Jasmine Rice

#mealprep #legomealprep #dietitian

title:
High Protein Mexican Cheesy Beef Burritos!🔥🥩🌯

OVER 50g of Protein! Easy High Protein Burrito Meal Prep 😋

Comment “Cookbook” and I’ll DM you a link to my High Protein Cookbook with 100+ recipes just like this one! 📕👨🏽‍🍳 

Makes 6 Burritos: 🌯🌯🌯🌯🌯🌯

Calories & Macros 📊
Per Burrito: 583 calories 
51g P | 57g C | 15g F

Taco beef 
- 800g lean ground beef (5% or less)
- Taco seasoning (see below) 
- 1 medium red onion (diced)
- 1 red bell pepper (diced)
- 200g fajita sauce (brand: old el paso)
- cooking spray

Taco seasoning (homemade)
- 2 tsp paprika
- 2 tsp garlic powder
- 1 tsp onion powder
- 1 tsp cayenne
- 1 tsp cumin
- 1 tsp oregano
- 2 tsp salt
- 1 tsp black pepper

Mexican red rice
- 15g light butter
- 200g washed rice
- ½ tsp garlic powder
- ½ tsp onion powder
- ½ tsp cayenne
- 1 tsp salt
- 35g tomato paste
- 400ml chicken stock (brand: oxo)

Other ingredients
- 6 protein tortillas (brand: mission) - sub with low carb tortillas
- 180g low fat cheese

Extra Notes ✍🏽
- toast in the pan (optionally with butter) folded side down to seal the burrito
- Allow the burritos to cool before wrapping in foil

Storage & Heating ♨️
- Wrap in foil and store in the fridge for up to a week or in the freezer for a couple months
- To reheat, remove the foil, wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave for 3-4 minutes from the fridge or 5-6 minutes from the freezer, flipping over at halfway, unwrap carefully from the paper towel air-fry or toast in the pan for a couple minutes to get crispy and enjoy!

title:
Bibimbap Meal Prep 101 (10 servings)

1 cup = 240ml
1 T = 15ml
1 t = 5ml

Ingredients for 10 servings

- Uncooked rice: 650g (3.5 cups)
- Bean sprouts 500g
- Spinach 300g
- 1 White radish (about 500g)
- 1 Carrot (300g)
- Mushrooms 400g (I used shiitake, but any sauté-friendly mushrooms work: button, king oyster, enoki, etc.)
- 1 Zucchini (500g)
- Minced garlic

⸻

🌶️ Yak-Gochujang ( Bibimbap Sauce )

Ingredients
- Ground pork 300g
- Minced garlic 3T
- Light soy sauce 2T (i used Sempio 701)
- Sugar 2T
- Gochujang 1 cup
- Water 400g
- Vinegar 2T (white or rice vinegar etc, i used rice vinegar)
- Sesame oil 2T

Recipe
1. Brown the ground pork over medium-high heat.
2. Add garlic and sauté for about 1 minute (don’t burn it).
3. Add soy sauce, sugar, and gochujang. Sauté for 1 minute. (Pour soy sauce along the edge of the pan to boost aroma.)
4. Add water and dissolve the gochujang.
5. Turn off heat. Once slightly cooled, mix in vinegar and sesame oil.

⸻

🥬 Banchan (Side Dishes)

1️⃣ Sautéed Zucchini
- Slice zucchini (fan shape or julienne)
- Sauté with 3T oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes
- Add salt (2g)
- Finish with 1t sesame oil

⸻

2️⃣ Sautéed Carrots
- Thinly julienne carrots
- Sauté with 3T oil for 3 minutes
- Add salt (2g)
- Finish with 1t sesame oil

⸻

3️⃣ Sautéed Mushrooms
- Slice mushrooms thinly
- Sauté with 3T oil for 4 minutes
- Add salt (2g) and black pepper
- Add 1t minced garlic at 3-minute mark
- Finish with 1t sesame oil

⸻

4️⃣ Bean Sprouts Namul
- Blanch bean sprouts for 1–2 minutes
- Mix with : Minced garlic 1T + Sesame oil 1T + 3 pinch of salt (4g)

⸻

5️⃣ Spinach Namul
- Blanch spinach for 30 seconds
- Rinse in cold water and squeeze dry
- Mix with   : pinch of salt (1g) + Minced garlic ½T + Sesame oil 1T

⸻

6️⃣ Mu-Saengchae
- White radish 500g (julienne shape)
- Gochugaru 2T (30g)
- Minced garlic 4T (60g)
- Minced ginger 10g (optional)
- Sugar 2T
- Salt 1T
- Chopped green onion (optional)
- Vinegar 1T
- Mix everything and let it sit for about 3 minutes.

⸻

🍱 How to Enjoy Bibimbap Meal Prep
- Fridge: Eat within 3–4 days → Microwave for 2–3 minutes before eating
- Freezer: Store longer-term if needed
- Feel free to swap or add any side dishes you like.
- Bibimbap is flexible — use what you love.

- 3 tbsp oil
- 1 onion
- 2 jalapeños,
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 inch ginger

- 1½ tsp garam masala

- 2(15-ounce) cans chickpeas, rinsed

- 1½ tsp salt
- ¾ cup chopped cilantro,
- lime juice

Sauté the onion, jalapeño, and bay leaf in a large skillet over medium-high heat until the onion edges are golden, then stir in the ginger, garlic, and ground spices (garam masala, cumin, and turmeric) until fragrant. Next, add the chickpeas, coconut milk, pumpkin, water, and salt, bringing the mixture to a simmer for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Once thickened, finish the curry by stirring in fresh cilantro and lime juice to taste, and serve warm over a bed of rice or couscous with extra lime wedges on the side.

title:
CHICKEN THAT DOESNT SUCK. This is one of the best 1 pan chicken recipes you’ll make. The secret is the marinate that will elevate the chicken and the quick garlicky herb sauce is unbelievably good! 

I’m using bone-in skin-on chicken thighs to make the chicken more flavorful and juicy, but you can remove the skin if you prefer, too.

I paired this with a simple salad, but it would be complete with some regular rice, quinoa, or if you’re doing lowcarb/keto, some of my lowcarb @kaizenfoodco rice.
.
This is how I made it (feel free to multiply for more)
.
1.Grab 4 skin-on bone-in chicken thighs, dab them dry with a paper towel and add them to a bowl.
.
2.For the marinade, grab a medium mixing bowl. Add 2 tbsp drizzle of olive oil, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 4 minced garlic cloves, the zest and juice of 1 large lemon, a couple generous pinches salt, pepper, 1 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp oregano or thyme, 1/4 to 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper. Mix it really well.
.
3.Add the marinade to the chicken, and mix really well covering all sides. Let this ideally sit for 2 to 6 or ideally, overnight.
.
4.Preheat oven to 410F. Remove chicken from fridge and let it come up to room temp before putting in the oven.
.
5.Place chicken on a wire rack and put it in the oven at 410F for 35-40 mins.
.
6.While thats going, make your sauce. I processed together 3 tablespoons of thick greek yogurt (or labneh), a handful of fresh mint (about 3 tablespoons), 2 scallions (green and white part), 1/2 large jalapeño, 1 tbsp olive oil, the juice of half a lemon, and a couple generous pinches of salt + pepper. Process well, taste, and adjust to your preference.
.
7.Remove the chicken from the oven, plate it. Again, you can serve this with whatever base you like (it would be delicious with regular rice, quinoa, or if you’re lowcarb/keto my high protein kaizen rice), some salad of choice, and this sauce.
.
If you make it, be sure to let me know on SHREDHAPPENS. ENJOY!
.
.
.
.

title:
Hassle back potatoes with creamy Cajun chicken and airfried brocollini . Easy, healthy comfort meal 

Potato recipe
6 medium potatoes
3 tbsp butter (melted)
2 tbsp olive oil
4–5 cloves garlic (minced)
1½ tsp paprika
1½ tsp onion granules
1½ tsp garlic granules
1 tsp dried parsley
Salt & pepper
1–2 tsp all-purpose seasoning
Method:
Slice each potato thinly (don’t cut all the way through).
Mix melted butter, olive oil, garlic, and all seasonings.
Brush generously over all 6 potatoes, getting into the layers.
Air fry at 180°C for 35–45 mins (depending on size).
Brush with extra butter halfway through for that crispy finish.

Chicken recipe 
Ingredients:
1 tbsp olive oil
1½ tsp Cajun seasoning
½ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper
1 tsp paprika
1 tsp onion powder
Method:
Add the sliced chicken to a bowl.
Drizzle over the olive oil.
Sprinkle all the seasonings evenly.
Mix well until every piece is fully coated.
Let it sit for 10–15 minutes (optional, but boosts flavor).
Pan-fry on medium-high heat until golden and cooked through.

Cajun Sauce:
1 tbsp butter
½ onion (diced)
150–200ml heavy cream
Same seasonings as chicken
Instructions 
In the same pan, melt butter and cook onions until soft.
Add cream + seasoning, simmer until thickened.
Add chicken back in and coat in sauce.

title:
Cabbage Rolls 🥬#sugarfree #lowcarb #prediabetes

Healthy and delicious cabbage rolls that are sugar-free and super low in carbs. Perfect for a complete dinner that keeps my husband's glucose stable and leaves us feeling super satisfied.

INGREDIENTS:
🥬 Filling:
8 oz white button mushrooms, diced
1 lb ground chicken
3 green onions (white parts chopped for the filling, green parts for garnish)
4 large garlic cloves, minced
1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce (or coconut aminos)
⅛ tsp sesame oil
⅛ tsp ginger powder
1 tsp salt (or to taste)
Pinch of black pepper
Avocado oil for cooking

🥢 Sauce:
2 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
1 tbsp allulose
1 tsp rice vinegar
¼ tsp sesame oil
⅛ tsp garlic powder
1 tsp green onions (green parts), diced
Pinch of black pepper

✨ For Assembly & Serving:
1 large Napa cabbage
Sesame seeds and the green parts of the green onions for garnish

Instructions:
1. FILLING: Heat a drizzle of avocado oil in a skillet. Add the diced mushrooms with a little salt and cook until they have released all their water. Add the white parts of the green onions and the garlic, and cook for another minute. Season with pepper, ginger powder, and soy sauce. Add the ground chicken and cook until it is well done. Remove from the heat and stir in the sesame oil.

2. CABBAGE: While the filling is cooking, boil the cabbage leaves in water for about 5-10 minutes, or until the white part is tender and bendy. Carefully remove them and pat them very dry with a paper towel.

3. ASSEMBLE & COOK: Place about 1 ½ tablespoons of filling on each cabbage leaf and roll it up. In a clean skillet over medium-high heat, pan-fry the rolls on all sides until golden brown.

4. SAUCE & SERVING: In a small bowl, mix all the sauce ingredients. Serve the rolls hot, pour the sauce over them, and garnish with the green parts of the green onions and sesame seeds.

title:
High-protein chicken Alfredo bake 🤍
This is SO creamy and decadent you’d never guess it’s a lighter swap… and it comes together in no time! .

High-Protein Chicken Alfredo Bake

Ingredients (Serves ~6)

* 2-3 cups steamed broccoli (bite-size, cooked until al dente)
* ~20 oz cooked rotisserie chicken breast, shredded or chopped
* 160g Trader Joe’s Lite Shredded Mozzarella (about 1 ⅓ cups), divided
* 2.5 oz grated Parmesan cheese, divided

Sauce:

* 1 (15 oz) jar Rao’s Alfredo Sauce
* 1 cup Fairlife Reduced Fat Milk
* 1 cup (8 oz) Good Culture Low-Fat Cottage Cheese
* garlic powder, to taste
* onion powder, to taste
* salt, to taste
* black pepper, to taste

⸻

Instructions

1. Preheat oven to 375°F.
2. Add steamed broccoli to the bottom of a 10x7 casserole dish.
3. Sprinkle half of the mozzarella and Parmesan over the broccoli.
4. Layer the cooked chicken evenly on top.
5. In a bowl, mix together the Alfredo sauce, milk, cottage cheese, and seasonings until smooth and well combined.
6. Pour the sauce evenly over the casserole, gently poking around so it settles throughout (no need to fully mix).
7. Top with the remaining mozzarella and Parmesan.
8. Bake uncovered for 35 minutes, or until hot and bubbly.
9. Broil for 2–3 minutes until the top is golden and slightly crispy.

⸻

Calories & Macros (per serving, ~6 servings)

* Calories: ~385
* Protein: ~47g
* Carbs: ~8–10g
* Fat: ~18g

(Will vary slightly depending on exact chicken + cheese brands)

title:
Double Chocolate Banana Bread 🍫🍌 A healthier banana bread recipe with all the chocolate flavors you could ask for - and honestly, it might be the best banana bread I've ever made.

I love having a sweet treat at home that I can enjoy as a daily dessert. Balance isn't about restriction, it's about finding recipes like this that satisfy your cravings with better ingredients.

Ingredients:
* 2 very ripe bananas
* 50g butter or coconut oil, melted
* 120ml milk of choice
* 1 tsp vanilla extract
* 190g flour
* 1 tsp baking soda
* 1/4 tsp salt
* 40g cocoa powder
* 100g coconut sugar or brown sugar
* 1 chia egg (1 tbsp chia seeds + 3 tbsp water)
* 100g chocolate chunks

Instructions: 

Preheat oven to 175°C and line your loaf pan with baking paper.

Prepare your chia egg and set aside.

Mash the bananas, then add the melted butter or oil, milk, and vanilla. Mix until smooth.

In another bowl, sift the flour and cocoa powder. Add baking soda, sugar, and salt. Mix well.

Add the chia egg and dry ingredients to the wet mixture. Whisk gently until smooth but don't overmix.

Fold in chocolate chunks and pour into the loaf tin.

Bake for 40-55 minutes. Test at 40 minutes with a knife - if it comes out clean, it's ready.

Let it cool completely before slicing or you'll have a delicious mess on your hands and a crumbled cake in front of you

title:
Crispy Rice Salad 🍚🥗

Crunchy, fresh, creamy, spicy… this Crispy Rice Salad has EVERYTHING

INGREDIENTS
Crispy Rice:
1 cup cold, cooked rice (day-old for best texture)
1 tbsp chili oil
1 tsp soy sauce

Salad Base:
1 cups cucumbers, thinly sliced
1 avocado, sliced 
1 cup cooked shrimp or protein of your choice
1/2 cup shelled edamame (cooked)
1-2 green onions, thinly sliced

Optional Add-Ins:
Fresh herbs: cilantro or mint
Lime wedges, for serving
Sesame seeds 

Peanut Dressing:
1/2 cup peanut butter
1 tbsp rice vinegar
1 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
1/2 tbsp toasted sesame oil
2 garlic cloves, finely minced
1-2 tbsp warm water (to loosen)

⸻

INSTRUCTIONS
Rice → Toss rice with chili oil, and soy sauce. Spread in a thin layer on parchment and air fryer at 400°F (200°C) for 14-18 minutes, until deep golden and crispy edges.

Dressing → Whisk everything until smooth and pourable. Add water slowly until it’s creamy but not thick.
*Taste check: salty + sweet + tangy + nutty. Adjust with lime or honey if needed.

Salad → In a large bowl, combine all salad ingredients.

Finish → Fold in the crispy rice last so it stays crunchy. Drizzle dressing on top. Finish with herbs, sesame seeds, and a squeeze of lime.

⸻

title:
this baked feta, chicken & quinoa with veggies has over 8 million views and so many remakes…for good reason!! it’s so easy, delish, & makes for perfect leftovers 🍅🍃🥦    

here’s everything you need:
- 1 cup (8oz) feta cheese (block is best but crumbled works)

- 1 +1/2 lbs boneless chicken breast
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 2 tsp garlic powder

- 1 cup cooked quinoa

Preheat oven to 400 degrees. In a large casserole dish, add the feta block, olive oil, cherry tomatoes, broccoli, and chicken, spacing the chicken evenly and placing the feta in the middle.

Mix everything together well in the casserole dish without the chicken, then add in the basil and quinoa and stir again.

Add the chicken back in, top with some extra oil and basil if desired, and serve. The recipe makes 4 servings and stores well in the refrigerator for 3-4 days in an airtight container.

enjoy!! 💕
